```{r}
# match_counties_to_uscrn.R
# Purpose: match each county (reliability sf) to the nearest USCRN station (WBANNO) extracted
#          from a big sub-hourly uscrn_combined_reformatted.rds table.
#
# Requirements: sf, dplyr, readr
# Run: Adjust file paths as needed and run in your R session.

library(sf)
library(dplyr)
library(readr)

# --------------------- Inputs - adjust paths ---------------------
# Your reliability sf (if already in memory, assign it to sf_reliability and skip st_read)
# sf_reliability <- reliability_metrics_table_final
# OR read from gpkg:
gpkg_path <- "./data_processed/reliability_metrics_table_final.gpkg"
sf_reliability <- st_read(dsn = gpkg_path, quiet = TRUE)

# Weather RDS containing sub-hour observations and station IDs
uscrn_rds <- "./data_processed/uscrn_combined_reformatted.rds"

# Output paths
out_gpkg <- "./data_processed/reliability_with_matched_uscrn.gpkg"
out_lookup_csv <- "./data_processed/county_to_uscrn_lookup.csv"

# --------------------- Load weather data (big RDS) ---------------------
message("Reading RDS...")
uscrn <- readRDS(uscrn_rds)   # expects a data.frame / tibble

# Quick check that WBANNO exists
if (!"WBANNO" %in% names(uscrn)) stop("WBANNO column not found in uscrn RDS. Check column names.")

# --------------------- Extract unique station locations ---------------------
lon_names <- "LONGITUDE"
lat_names <- "LATITUDE"

lon_col <- intersect(names(uscrn), lon_names) %>% first()
lat_col <- intersect(names(uscrn), lat_names) %>% first()

if (is.null(lon_col) || is.null(lat_col)) {
  stop("Could not auto-detect lon/lat columns in uscrn. Edit lon_names/lat_names or rename columns.")
}

message(paste0("Using lon/lat columns: ", lon_col, " , ", lat_col))

# Keep only unique stations by WBANNO (and coordinates). If a station has slightly varying coords,
# we take the median coordinate by WBANNO to be robust.
stations_unique <- uscrn %>%
  group_by(WBANNO) %>%
  summarize(
    station_lon = median(.data[[lon_col]], na.rm = TRUE),
    station_lat = median(.data[[lat_col]], na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(station_lon) & !is.na(station_lat))

# Convert to sf (WGS84 assumed). If your lon/lat are already in a different CRS, change crs accordingly.
sf_stations <- st_as_sf(stations_unique, coords = c("station_lon", "station_lat"), crs = 4326, remove = FALSE)

# --------------------- Prepare reliability centroids ---------------------
# We'll use centroids of the reliability geometries for nearest-station matching.
# Transform both datasets to a projected CRS in meters for distance calculations.
proj_crs <- 3857   # Web Mercator; swap to local projection for better accuracy if needed

sf_reliability_centroid <- sf_reliability %>%
  st_transform(crs = proj_crs) %>%
  mutate(.centroid = st_centroid(st_geometry(.))) %>%
  st_set_geometry(".centroid")   # sets the centroid as the active geometry

sf_stations_proj <- st_transform(sf_stations, crs = proj_crs)

# --------------------- Find nearest station per county ---------------------
# st_nearest_feature -> index in sf_stations_proj for each county
nearest_idx <- st_nearest_feature(sf_reliability_centroid, sf_stations_proj)

# Pull matched station rows and compute distances
stations_matched <- sf_stations_proj[nearest_idx, , drop = FALSE]

# Compute distances (meters)
dists <- st_distance(st_geometry(sf_reliability_centroid), st_geometry(stations_matched), by_element = TRUE)
dist_m <- as.numeric(units::set_units(dists, "m"))

# --------------------- Build final joined object ---------------------
# Station attributes to attach (drop geometry), prefix to avoid collisions
stations_attrs <- stations_matched %>%
  st_drop_geometry() %>%
  rename_with(~ paste0("station_", .), everything())

# Bind columns to the original reliability (keep original geometry & attributes)
sf_reliability_with_uscrn <- sf_reliability %>%
  mutate(nearest_station_idx = nearest_idx,
         nearest_station_distance_m = dist_m) %>%
  bind_cols(stations_attrs)

# --------------------- Optional: thresholding by distance ---------------------
# Mark if the matched station is within a reasonable distance (e.g., 50 km). Adjust as needed.
max_allow_m <- 50000  # 50 km
sf_reliability_with_uscrn <- sf_reliability_with_uscrn %>%
  mutate(station_within_50km = nearest_station_distance_m <= max_allow_m)

# --------------------- Output: save lookup and gpkg ---------------------
# Save GeoPackage with matched info (geometry preserved)
st_write(sf_reliability_with_uscrn, dsn = out_gpkg, layer = "reliability_with_uscrn", delete_dsn = TRUE, quiet = TRUE)

# Create a minimal lookup table: county identifiers -> WBANNO (station ID) and distance
# Adjust the selecting columns below to include the county/state identifiers you want
lookup <- sf_reliability_with_uscrn %>%
  st_drop_geometry() %>%
  transmute(
    state = state,                # modify if your column has a different name
    county = county,              # modify if your column has a different name
    WBANNO = station_WBANNO,
    nearest_station_distance_m,
    station_within_50km
  )

readr::write_csv(lookup, out_lookup_csv)

message("Saved matched GeoPackage: ", out_gpkg)
message("Saved county -> WBANNO lookup CSV: ", out_lookup_csv)

# --------------------- Quick checks / examples ---------------------
# Show a few matched rows to sanity check
print( sf_reliability_with_uscrn %>%
         st_drop_geometry() %>%
         select(state, county, station_WBANNO, nearest_station_distance_m) %>%
         slice_head(n = 10) )

# If you later want to pull all weather rows for the matched station for regression,
# you can inner_join on WBANNO:
#
# example_station_ids <- unique(lookup$WBANNO)
# weather_for_these <- uscrn %>% filter(WBANNO %in% example_station_ids)
#
# But for big regressions, it's often best to:
# - left_join the lookup table onto your county-level panel by date/station,
# - or aggregate station-level time series to daily/hourly features first, then merge.
#
# --------------------- End ---------------------


```
